subject.title: fix(memory-core): make dream narrative timeout configurable

question: Should memory-core expose a persistent `dreaming.execution.*.timeoutMs` operator control, with default-to-phase inheritance, rather than keep the 60-second narrative wait as fixed behavior?
rationale: The current implementation has no supported config path, while repository policy sets a high bar for new config surfaces and requires maintainers to choose the durable plugin contract.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow timeout control
options.body: Approve the timeout setting at the memory-core owner boundary, then require a rebased patch that limits resolver changes to `timeoutMs` and proves an actual configured narrative run.

options.title: Keep a fixed timeout
options.body: Decline the new config contract and address slow-model reliability through the existing Dreaming concurrency/no-tools work instead.

options.title: Decide in the canonical issue
options.body: Use the broader open Dream Diary reliability report to settle timeout, concurrency, and disablement semantics before accepting any partial implementation.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow timeout control
recommendation.body: Approve the timeout setting at the memory-core owner boundary, then require a rebased patch that limits resolver changes to `timeoutMs` and proves an actual configured narrative run.

likelyOwner.reason: Current timeout and related memory-core configuration history show the strongest direct ownership signal.
